title: The Euclidean closest vector problem

problem.name: The Euclidean closest vector problem
problem.statement_latex: Given a rank-$n$ lattice $L=B\mathbb Z^n$ and target $t\in\mathbb Q^m$, output $v\in L$ minimizing $\|v-t\|_2$. CVP models noisy lattice decoding and underlies attacks on lattice cryptography. The tree comparison counts quantum and classical node-oracle operations; total algorithms use quantum gates and classical bit operations including lattice arithmetic.
problem.statement_text: Given a rank-$n$ lattice $L=B\mathbb Z^n$ and target $t\in\mathbb Q^m$, output $v\in L$ minimizing $\|v-t\|_2$. quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(\sqrt T\,\operatorname{poly}(n))$ node operations, quantum lattice enumeration.
quantum.details_latex: Here $T$ is the size of the classical enumeration tree for the chosen basis and search radius, and its depth is $n$. Radius refinement and witness recovery introduce polynomial factors. The arithmetic cost also depends on basis bit length and precision. This bound gives a matched acceleration of the specified tree, while general exact CVP can also be solved by running the classical $2^{n+o(n)}$ algorithm on quantum hardware.

classical.headline_latex: $2^{n+o(n)}$ time and space, Aggarwal--Dadush--Stephens-Davidowitz exact CVP; $T$ nodes for the matched enumeration tree.
classical.details_latex: The general exact algorithm uses discrete-Gaussian sampling and a reduction through clusters of approximate closest vectors. For the promise $\operatorname{dist}(t,L)\le\alpha\lambda_1(L)$ with $\alpha<1.039\ldots$, Hhan gives $2^{n/2+o(n)}$ classical time and space. Its lattice model and distance guarantee are part of that bound. The appropriate comparator is the minimum of the general, promised-distance and enumeration bounds applicable to the input.

strength.description_latex: Quadratic acceleration in enumeration-tree size. The total-runtime comparison with the best classical solver depends on $T$, basis quality and the target-distance promise.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous quantum backtracking upper bounds; partial evidence for separation from optimized classical CVP algorithms on explicit lattices.

hardware.description_latex: Quantum enumeration needs polynomial logical registers for coefficient prefixes and reversible arithmetic, but potentially exponential coherent depth. Discrete-Gaussian and list-based methods use exponential storage. Large cryptanalytic instances require fault tolerance.
